history.dynasty: Panchkot kings (per local tradition); earlier tradition credits Maharaja Hari Gupt
history.period: Claimed 3rd-century CE origins (unverified); renovated ~500 years ago; present structure built by Sri Gurudin Prasad Pal (modern era)
history.summary: 500-year-old centre of Shakti worship on the banks of the Barakar River, about 5 km downstream of Maithon Dam. Local tradition claims the first structure was built by Maharaja Hari Gupt of Panchkot in the 3rd century CE while fleeing the Kushanas; the ruined temple was renovated by the king of Panchkot about five centuries ago over five years, and the present structure was constructed by Sri Gurudin Prasad Pal. It is regarded locally as a Shakti Peeth (not among the classical 51), and legend says human sacrifices were offered here in the remote past. The goddess is believed to be a living deity who fulfills the wishes of childless women. FLAG - town corrected: the temple stands at Kalyaneshwari, ~20 km from Asansol (not in Asansol city). Dating conflict between the 3rd-century origin claim and the 500-year documented history is unresolved.

name: Kalyaneshwari Temple
town_description: Kalyaneshwari is a census town and pilgrimage locality in the Asansol Sadar subdivision of Paschim Bardhaman district, right on the West Bengal-Jharkhand border. It sits on the Barakar River just downstream of the Maithon Dam and grew up around the famous Shakti temple; devotees and day-trippers from Asansol, Dhanbad and Durgapur visit regularly.

travel.airport: Kazi Nazrul Islam Airport (Andal/Durgapur), ~50 km - verify.
travel.railway: Barakar railway station is the nearest; Asansol Junction is ~20-23 km away.
travel.road: On the old Grand Trunk Road near Barakar town, about 1 km off NH-2; regular bus services from Asansol, Durgapur and Dhanbad.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March - cooler, less humid weather ideal for sightseeing and worship.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented from a reliable source - verify before visiting.
